title: River Review fast-verification checkpoint evidence
description: Evidence produced by one `after-change` fast-verification checkpoint (#2275 PR-3B, Epic #2054 Phase 3). It records what was verified about one subject revision and, just as importantly, what was NOT: `pass` is reserved for a deterministic check that really ran and really succeeded, and every other outcome keeps its own word (`fail`, `unrunnable`, `skipped`, `bypassed`, `stale`). This document carries no host vocabulary — hook names, tool names and invocation mechanics belong to the adapter — and no judgment: it starts no Flow, applies no severity, and changes no gate, decision or merge authority. It also carries no raw process output: only the bounded execution metadata the deterministic orchestrator preserves (#2275 PR-3A).

triggerId.description: Neutral trigger id this checkpoint answers for. Only `after-change` starts no Flow and declares the fast-verification profile.

occurrenceKey.description: `<occurrenceId>@<subjectRevision>`. An occurrence is the same occurrence only on the same subject revision; a re-send under this key is recorded as `skipped` / `duplicate-occurrence` rather than run again.

subjectRevision.description: Commit SHA or content hash the checkpoint is about. A verdict that outlives this revision is `stale`, never `pass`.

profile.description: Verification profile. `fast-verification` means changed-file-scoped deterministic checks with no network call, no model call and no full test suite.

mode.description: Rollout mode. `observe` only: this evidence informs nobody's gate and blocks nothing.

changedFiles.description: Repo-relative paths the change touched, normalized and sorted. The scope the checks were run against; an empty list means there was nothing to verify.

checks.description: One row per deterministic check this occurrence was accountable for — including the checks that did not run, which is what keeps a non-execution from reading as a success.

status.description: Checkpoint-level roll-up: the worst outcome present, ordered stale > fail > unrunnable > bypassed > skipped > pass, so no non-verdict can be summarized as a pass.

reasonCode.description: Why the checkpoint ended as it did.

totalDurationMs.description: Wall-clock duration of the checkpoint, used for the dogfood p50/p95 measurement in PR-3D.

id.description: Skill id that declared the deterministic check.

status.description: pass = ran and succeeded on this revision. fail = ran and reported failure. unrunnable = attempted, no verdict (spawn error, timeout, invalid entry, an executor status that cannot be read, or results that cannot be attributed to the gates that produced them). skipped = nothing to run (no check selected, no changed file, duplicate occurrence). bypassed = running was not permitted (no host-trusted allowlist, an unusable one, or this exact argv is not on it). stale = a verdict exists but may not be read as a verdict on the subject, because the subject revision moved or could not be confirmed afterwards.

supersededStatus.description: The verdict that was produced before it was refused: on a `stale` row, before the subject moved; on an `unrunnable` / `staging-incomplete` / `staging-evidence-missing` row, the `pass` that could not be confirmed against the sandbox the check actually ran in. Kept so the run is auditable, and deliberately NOT promoted back into `status`.

stdoutBytes.description: Byte count only. Raw stdout / stderr is never persisted as evidence.

staging.description: What reached the sandbox this check ran in (#2311). A check runs against copies of the changed files, and the sandbox refuses a symlinked, escaping or `.git` path; a checker handed a sandbox missing one of its subject files still exits 0. `complete: false` therefore means the run says nothing about the files listed in `skipped`, and the row's `pass` is recorded as `unrunnable` instead. Repo-relative paths only; copy-error messages are never persisted.

deleted.description: Changed files the caller DECLARED the change deleted. They are not staged and do not count towards `requested`, because a removed file is not in the review source tree and would otherwise make every deleting change permanently `unrunnable`. Declared by the caller only: absence from the source tree is never read as deletion, since an empty or wrong source tree would then read as a clean run.
